stem.presentation: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, not on Coumadin after a prior INR of 18, presented with severe dry mouth after starting a BPH medication. In the ED, he developed AF with RVR to the 130–140s and received multiple IV/PO diltiazem doses with partial improvement. He had mild AKI and received 2 L normal saline. On the floor, his heart rate remained difficult to control with IV/PO nodal-blocking agents, and he developed worsening hypoxia, wheezing, and confusion. IV furosemide 40 mg ×2 produced minimal response, prompting transfer to the CCU for persistent AF with RVR and worsening CHF.

stem.presentation: An 83-year-old man with chronic diastolic CHF with EF 50–55%, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, sick sinus syndrome/complete heart block status post pacemaker, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes presented with 1 week of progressive dyspnea on exertion and orthopnea. He denied chest pain, chest pressure, and peripheral edema, though he felt his legs were heavier. He reported adherence to diuretics and a low-sodium diet, but his bumetanide had recently been reduced from 2 mg PO BID to 2 mg PO daily by nephrology; the exact timing was not specified/redacted in the extracted source row. He denied prior stroke, TIA, DVT, PE, bleeding at surgery, cough, hemoptysis, black/red stools, fevers, chills, rigors, exertional leg pain, syncope, or presyncope. In the ED, ECG was at baseline, CXR showed a moderate-to-large right pleural effusion, BNP was 9170 from baseline 6019, and TnT was 0.06. He received no ED medications or interventions and was admitted to Cardiology for presumed CHF exacerbation.

stem.presentation: A 75-year-old woman with non-small cell lung cancer previously treated with chemotherapy and radiation, COPD, and hypertension presents for her third episode of dyspnea and hemoptysis. During an earlier hospitalization, bronchoscopy showed generalized submucosal inflammation without endobronchial lesions or a clear source of injury. During a subsequent admission, she improved with COPD treatment and was discharged with scheduled inhalers and a five-day course of cefpodoxime and azithromycin for community-acquired pneumonia. Her ambulatory oxygen saturation at that discharge was 93–97% on room air. After one day at home, she developed worsening dyspnea after walking back from the bathroom. She reported eating a large meal earlier that evening. Her cough had generally improved, although intermittent rusty sputum persisted. She denied chest pain, palpitations, or diaphoresis. She also reported recent left ankle swelling and pain that improved after taking an unspecified “arthritis pill.” In the ED, she received bronchodilators, methylprednisolone, vancomycin, piperacillin- tazobactam, aspirin, and IV fluids in anticipation of CT angiography. She was subsequently admitted to the hospital floor.

stem.presentation: A 52-year-old man with multiple sclerosis, wheelchair dependence, and a strong family history of premature CAD presented with chest heaviness beginning shortly after his usual wheelchair-based exercise routine. The discomfort radiated to his neck, jaw, left ear, and left arm, improved transiently, then recurred at work. Two sublingual nitroglycerin tablets nearly resolved his symptoms. His PCP referred him to the ED, where the initial ECG was unremarkable and the initial cardiac enzymes were described as negative. He received aspirin and metoprolol and was started on a heparin infusion, after which he remained pain-free. He denied dyspnea, orthopnea, edema, palpitations, or syncope.

stem.presentation: A 91-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presented with two weeks of palpitations, one week of dyspnea, and two days of worsening lower-extremity edema. She was referred to the ED after a home assessment found a heart rate in the 130s. In the ED, her heart rate was in the 140s with a regular narrow-complex tachycardia. IV diltiazem slowed the rate. She received 500 mL of IV fluid while the rhythm was being clarified, then developed an oxygen requirement and received IV furosemide. Additional IV and oral diltiazem controlled the rate and resolved the palpitations. An elevated D-dimer prompted CTA, which was negative for pulmonary embolism.

stem.presentation: A 69-year-old man with CAD, CHF with a previous LVEF of 45%, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and OSA presented with progressive dyspnea beginning the previous evening. Symptoms worsened overnight, with exertion and when supine. He reported medication and dietary nonadherence, increased water intake, and fluid retention. He denied chest pain, palpitations, fever, or dizziness. ED examination showed volume overload, and bedside echocardiography showed global hypokinesis with an LVEF of approximately 25%. He received IV furosemide, sublingual nitroglycerin, and aspirin and was admitted for CHF management and ischemia evaluation. Dyspnea improved but had not returned to baseline on the floor.

Subsequent CXR: Mild cardiomegaly, pulmonary vascular congestion, interstitial edema, and trace bilateral pleural effusions.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic systolic HF; HFrEF, LVEF 27%, NYHA class III.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Medication nonadherence, CAD and nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.
OTHER PROBLEMS: Diabetes with hyperglycemia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral vascular disease, OSA and first-degree AV block.

acute.text: START: IV furosemide for volume overload; potassium chloride for hypokalemia.
HOLD: Isosorbide mononitrate during acute decompensation and ARNI transition.

gdmt.text: STOP: Lisinopril; START: Sacubitril-valsartan after a 36-hour washout.
TITRATE UP: Spironolactone; START: Dapagliflozin.
CONTINUE: Metoprolol succinate, atorvastatin, aspirin, amlodipine, insulin and heparin for VTE prophylaxis.
STOP: Omeprazole; CONTINUE: Pantoprazole.

monitor.text: MONITOR: Potassium with RAAS therapy, spironolactone and supplementation; renal function every 3 days during dapagliflozin initiation.
REQUEST: Formal transthoracic echocardiogram with Doppler assessment; iron studies (ferritin, TSAT).
SAFETY: Maintain at least 36 hours between stopping lisinopril and starting sacubitril-valsartan.

dispo.text: OUTPATIENT: Cardiac MRI with late gadolinium enhancement; reassess LVEF after 3 months of optimized GDMT and adherence.
DISCUSS: Goals of care and ICD implantation in the setting of DNR status.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic systolic HF.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: Previous LVEF 45%; bedside LVEF approximately 25%, formal resting study 27%.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Medication and dietary nonadherence; excess water intake.
ACTIVE PROBLEMS: Volume overload, orthopnea, hypertension and hyperglycemia.
HISTORY: CAD, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, peripheral vascular disease and OSA.

acute.text: START: IV furosemide, sublingual nitroglycerin and aspirin in the ED.

gdmt.text: START: Torsemide, spironolactone, metoprolol and isosorbide.
START: Omeprazole and obecabtagene autoleucel.

monitor.text: OBTAIN: ECG, bedside echocardiography, chest radiography and serial troponins; troponin negative twice.
OBTAIN: Stress echocardiography with resting LVEF 27%, improving to 40% after exercise.
MONITOR: No recommendation.

stem.presentation: A 49-year-old man with a seizure disorder and asthma presented with sudden palpitations beginning that morning after drinking a cold soda. Several hours later, he developed lightheadedness and near-syncope. He denied chest pain or dyspnea. He reported recent URI symptoms, an asthma flare, and increased albuterol use over the preceding three days. Clinic evaluation identified atrial flutter, prompting ED referral. In the ED, the ventricular rate was approximately 150 bpm. Two IV diltiazem doses were followed by conversion to sinus rhythm and initiation of oral diltiazem. He also received IV fluids and aspirin. On the floor, he felt well and had no complaints.
stem.vitals: ED: afebrile, HR 147, BP 137/76, RR not provided, SpO₂ 100% on room air. Admission: T 98.5, HR 81, BP 114/66, RR 13, SpO₂ 97% on room air.
stem.labs: Following-morning results: troponin T <0.01 ng/mL | Na 140 mEq/L | K 4.1 mEq/L | Mg 2.0 mg/dL | BUN 11 mg/dL | Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL | Glucose 93 mg/dL | WBC 4.1 K/µL | Hgb 14.4 g/dL | Platelets 189 K/µL.
exam: No acute distress; alert and oriented. JVP 8 cm.
Regular rhythm, normal S1/S2, without murmurs, rubs, gallops, S3, or S4.
Bilateral expiratory wheezing with unlabored respirations.
No peripheral edema; abdomen soft and nontender.
echo: Normal left atrial size and normal RV size/free-wall motion; trivial mitral regurgitation.
Mild pulmonary artery systolic hypertension; no pericardial effusion.
The LV description is incomplete in the supplied extract; a numerical LVEF is not provided.
ecg: Initial tracing: Atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response and nonspecific ST–T changes; 2:1 AV conduction described in tracing summaries.
Repeat tracing: Sinus rhythm with a normal ECG; atrial flutter no longer present.
imaging: CXR: Clear lungs and normal cardiomediastinal contours; no pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: New-onset typical atrial flutter with rapid ventricular response.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: Not HF.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Acute URI and asthma exacerbation.
OTHER PROBLEMS: Palpitations, near-syncope, epilepsy, secondary pulmonary hypertension and hypertension.

acute.text: CONTINUE: Diltiazem for rate control; albuterol and ipratropium as needed for bronchospasm.
STOP: Aspirin and heparin.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: Montelukast, fluticasone-salmeterol, lamotrigine, phenytoin and multivitamin.

monitor.text: MONITOR: Rate-control response because phenytoin may reduce diltiazem exposure.
REQUEST: Phenytoin level and reassessment of antiepileptic regimen.

dispo.text: REFER: Outpatient electrophysiology consultation for cavotricuspid isthmus ablation.
FOLLOW-UP: Event monitor or 14-day Holter after discharge; spirometry after asthma exacerbation resolves.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Atrial flutter; rapid ventricular rate on presentation.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: No HF diagnosis recorded.

causes.text: ACTIVE PROBLEMS: Palpitations and presyncope; recent URI symptoms and increased albuterol use during an asthma flare.
HISTORY: Seizure disorder and asthma.

acute.text: START: IV diltiazem twice, followed by oral diltiazem; converted to sinus rhythm.
START: IV fluids and aspirin in the ED.

gdmt.text: START: None.
START: Oral diltiazem after conversion to sinus rhythm.

monitor.text: OBTAIN: ECG, chest radiograph and echocardiogram; no acute cardiopulmonary abnormality on chest radiograph.
MONITOR: No recommendation.

dispo.text: ADMIT: Hospital floor after ED treatment; comfortable and without complaints on arrival.

stem.presentation: A 74-year-old man with diabetes, CKD, CAD with prior MI and CABG, combined systolic and diastolic CHF, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was directly admitted with superficial left-foot ulcerations and increasing warmth, redness, and swelling extending into the ankle. He had chronic bilateral leg edema despite elevation, dressing changes, and diuresis. The left leg continued to worsen. He denied fever, chills, dyspnea, chest pain, or gastrointestinal symptoms.
stem.home_meds: Lisinopril, aspirin, furosemide, carvedilol, warfarin, atorvastatin.
stem.vitals: Admission: T 97.2, HR 82, BP 148/84, RR 18, SpO₂ 100% on room air.
stem.labs: Admission: NT-proBNP 30,367 pg/mL | Na 136 mEq/L | K 4.3 mEq/L | BUN 86 mg/dL | Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL | Glucose 147 mg/dL | WBC 5.9 K/µL | Hgb 12.0 g/dL | Platelets 223 K/µL | INR 2.8. Following-day results: troponin T 0.08 ng/mL twice | Lactate 2.4 mmol/L. Later admission trends: creatinine peak 3.1, last 2.4 mg/dL | BUN peak 114, last 103 mg/dL | INR range 1.9–3.1.
exam: Thin, emaciated man, alert and oriented, without acute distress.
JVP not elevated; lungs clear without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Irregularly irregular rhythm; normal S1/S2 without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Bilateral 2+ pitting edema to the upper tibiae with weeping.
Left-foot erythema, diminished sensation, and superficial plantar ulcerations at the toe tips; lower-extremity Doppler pulses were predominantly monophasic.
echo: Moderately dilated LV with severe global hypokinesis; LVEF 15%, slightly lower than the prior study.
Dilated RV with depressed free-wall contractility.
Moderately dilated left atrium and markedly dilated right atrium; estimated right atrial pressure at least 15 mmHg.
Mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation and mild pulmonary artery systolic hypertension; no LV thrombus or pericardial effusion.
ecg: AF with a controlled ventricular response and ventricular premature beats.
Nonspecific intraventricular conduction delay of LBBB type and diffuse nonspecific ST–T abnormalities.
imaging: CXR: Cardiomegaly, prominent main pulmonary artery, and increased perihilar vascularity concerning for pulmonary edema; no pneumothorax.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic systolic HF with acute decompensation; stage D HFrEF.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: LVEF 15%; right-sided HF also identified.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: Left lower-limb cellulitis and AF.
OTHER PROBLEMS: CKD stage 4, CAD/prior MI, diabetes with hyperglycemia, secondary pulmonary hypertension and left bundle-branch conduction delay.

acute.text: TITRATE UP: IV furosemide for severe volume overload; HOLD: Oral torsemide.
CONTINUE: Vancomycin, cephalexin and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for cellulitis.
CONTINUE: Insulin and acetaminophen.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: Lisinopril, carvedilol, warfarin, atorvastatin and aspirin; reassess aspirin need with anticoagulation.
START: Spironolactone deferred until trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is completed,.
START: Dapagliflozin deferred until after the acute phase,.
STOP: Potassium chloride.

monitor.text: MONITOR: Daily BMP, potassium and creatinine during aggressive diuresis and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole treatment.
CHECK: INR within 3 days because of warfarin–trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole interaction.
SAFETY: Hyperkalemia concerns with CKD, lisinopril, spironolactone and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole; renal monitoring during dapagliflozin initiation.
REQUEST: Formal 12-lead ECG with QRS duration measurement.

dispo.text: REFER: Advanced HF center for transplant/LVAD evaluation.
CONSULT: Palliative care for goals-of-care discussion.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic HF.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: LVEF 15%; dilated RV with depressed systolic function.

causes.text: PRESENTING PROBLEMS: Left-foot ulcerations with warmth, erythema and swelling extending up the ankle; refractory bilateral leg edema.
OTHER PROBLEMS: AF, CKD stage 4, AKI and malnutrition/cachexia.
HISTORY: CAD with prior MI/CABG, diabetes, hypertension and hyperlipidemia.

acute.text: START: Torsemide, potassium chloride, cephalexin and sulfamethoxazole. Acute IV diuretic or antibiotic administration is not documented.

gdmt.text: START: Nystatin, miconazole, docusate, sodium chloride, calcium carbonate and psyllium.

monitor.text: OBTAIN: Echocardiogram showing severe biventricular dysfunction; chest radiograph concerning for pulmonary edema.
MONITOR: No recommendation.

dispo.text: ADMIT: Direct inpatient admission for left-foot ulcerations, erythema and swelling with persistent edema.

stem.presentation: A 52-year-old man with hyperlipidemia, glucose intolerance, and a history of atypical chest pain developed several days of sharp, deep left-sided chest pain that worsened with inspiration, bending, and pulling movements and was partly reproducible. He denied dyspnea, nausea, diaphoresis, or radiation. At a scheduled exercise stress-test visit, the resting echocardiogram showed apical wall-motion abnormalities and global hypokinesis with an LVEF of 30%; exercise testing was not performed. He was sent for cardiac catheterization, which showed no coronary stenoses but identified an LAD-to-pulmonary-artery fistula without an oxygen-saturation step-up. He was transferred to the floor for monitoring.
stem.vitals: Admission after catheterization: T 98.8, HR 72, BP 109/71, RR 18, SpO₂ 99% on room air.
stem.labs: First available chemistry, the morning after admission: troponin T <0.01 ng/mL | Na 140 mEq/L | K 4.2 mEq/L | Mg 2.2 mg/dL | BUN 11 mg/dL | Creatinine 0.9 mg/dL | Glucose 136 mg/dL. Later CBC/coagulation: WBC 6.4 K/µL | Hgb 15.8 g/dL | Platelets 271 K/µL | INR 1.1. LDL 143 is recorded in the history.
exam: Lying flat after catheterization; JVP not assessed because of positioning.
Regular rhythm with normal S1/S2 and no murmurs, rubs, gallops, S3, or S4.
Lungs clear anteriorly; abdomen soft and nontender.
No peripheral edema, cyanosis, or clubbing.
echo: Normal LV size and wall thickness with moderate-to-severe global hypokinesis; LVEF 30%.
Severe hypokinesis of the apical third and mild hypokinesis of the basal third.
Normal RV size/function; mild mitral regurgitation, normal estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure, and no pericardial effusion.
Reported differential for the contraction pattern included coronary disease, stress- induced cardiomyopathy, and focal myopericarditis.
ecg: Narrative tracing: Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, normal intervals and axis, without ST–T changes.
Additional tracing summaries include AF with rapid ventricular response; their timing relative to presentation is not specified.
imaging: CXR: Normal cardiomediastinal contours and clear lungs; no pneumothorax or pleural effusion.
cath: Normal hemodynamics and no oxygen-saturation step-up in the clinical narrative.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: New nonischemic cardiomyopathy with HFrEF, LVEF 30%; stress-induced cardiomyopathy versus acute myocarditis/myopericarditis.

causes.text: OTHER PROBLEMS: AF, coronary artery fistula, diabetes with hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, pleuritic chest pain and hypertension.

acute.text: START: Oral furosemide for volume management.
CONTINUE: IV heparin during anticoagulant transition; stop at least 6 hours before first apixaban dose,.

gdmt.text: STOP: Lisinopril and metoprolol tartrate; START: Sacubitril-valsartan and metoprolol succinate.
START: Spironolactone, dapagliflozin and atorvastatin.
STOP: Warfarin; START: Apixaban.
STOP: Ibuprofen; CONTINUE: Metformin.

monitor.text: REQUEST: Cardiac MRI with gadolinium, LGE and T2/STIR sequences; NT-proBNP; serial troponin; HbA1c.
MONITOR: Renal function at 3 days and 1 week after dapagliflozin initiation; potassium with spironolactone and sacubitril-valsartan.
SAFETY: Avoid concurrent heparin and apixaban; stop ibuprofen because of HF/renal concerns.

dispo.text: FOLLOW-UP: Repeat echocardiogram after 3 months of GDMT optimization.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: Systolic HF and cardiomyopathy.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: LVEF 30%; global hypokinesis with more severe apical involvement.

causes.text: ACTIVE PROBLEMS: Pleuritic, partly reproducible chest pain; LAD-to-pulmonary-artery fistula without an oxygen-saturation step-up.
OTHER PROBLEMS: AF, diabetes and hyperlipidemia.

acute.text: PERFORM: Cardiac catheterization after abnormal resting echocardiogram; planned exercise stress test was not performed. No acute decongestive treatment documented.

gdmt.text: START: Metoprolol, aspirin, warfarin, heparin, pravastatin and fish oils.
START: Metformin, regular human insulin, glucose and glucagon.

monitor.text: OBTAIN: Coronary angiography—no coronary stenoses; LAD-to-pulmonary-artery fistula and normal hemodynamics.
OBTAIN: Echocardiogram; pattern does not exclude stress-induced cardiomyopathy or focal myopericarditis.
MONITORING PLAN: Transferred to the floor for further monitoring; schedule not specified.

dispo.text: ADMIT: Hospital floor after catheterization for further monitoring.

stem.presentation: Case 10 An 86-year-old man with CAD status post CABG and LCx PCI, bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, and systolic CHF with an ICD presented to an outside hospital with one hour of intermittent, nonradiating, band-like substernal chest pain. He denied dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, or diaphoresis. An IV nitroglycerin infusion was titrated with marked improvement in pain; he also received aspirin, morphine, and hydromorphone. He was transferred for consideration of cardiac catheterization and was chest-pain free on arrival to the CCU.
stem.home_meds: Aspirin, clopidogrel, spironolactone, heparin, nitroglycerin, amiodarone.
stem.vitals: Outside hospital: T 97.7, HR 61, BP 127/68, RR 16, SpO₂ 95% (oxygen device not specified). CCU arrival: T 97.9, HR 61, BP 142/74, RR 10, SpO₂ 97% on 2 L oxygen.
stem.labs: Admission: troponin T 0.02 ng/mL, subsequently <0.01 on three measurements | Na 139 mEq/L | K 4.2 mEq/L | Mg 2.3 mg/dL | BUN 38 mg/dL | Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL | Glucose 116 mg/dL | WBC 11.2 K/µL | Hgb 14.3 g/dL | Platelets 202 K/µL | INR 4.6, peak 4.7, later 1.3.
exam: Well-developed elderly man in no acute distress; alert and oriented with appropriate mood and affect.
No scleral icterus, pallor, cyanosis, or xanthomas in the available extract.
Additional cardiopulmonary examination findings are not supplied.
echo: Mild symmetric LV hypertrophy and mildly dilated LV cavity with moderate-to-severe global hypokinesis; LVEF 25%.
Normal RV size and free-wall motion; no LV thrombus.
Well-seated bioprosthetic aortic valve with a normal gradient and mild aortic regurgitation.
Mild-to-moderate mitral regurgitation, at least mild pulmonary artery systolic hypertension, and mildly dilated aortic root/ascending aorta; no pericardial effusion.
ecg: Narrative report: Atrial and ventricular pacing without significant change from the preceding tracing.
Additional automated summaries contain differing conduction and ischemic interpretations without clear timing; these do not establish a new presenting ECG change.
imaging: CXR: No focal opacity, pneumothorax, or signs of overhydration; minimal costophrenic- angle blunting suggesting small pre-existing pleural effusions. Device leads unchanged.
cath: Three-vessel CAD; patent SVG-LAD and occluded SVG-OM graft.
Balloon angioplasty of the OM2 origin achieved normal flow, no apparent dissection, and less than 20% residual stenosis.
Mild systemic systolic hypertension on resting hemodynamic assessment.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: NSTEMI / unstable angina with successful percutaneous revascularization.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: Acute on chronic systolic HF; LVEF 25%, NYHA II–III.

causes.text: CONTRIBUTORS: CAD and bypass-graft failure.
OTHER PROBLEMS: Prior MI, AF, CKD stage 3, bioprosthetic aortic valve, ICD and prior CABG.

acute.text: STOP: IV nitroglycerin and heparin after the acute/periprocedural course.
CONTINUE: Sublingual nitroglycerin as needed; START: Oral furosemide as needed if congestion develops.
HOLD: Prednisone pending assessment of need; STOP: Morphine.

gdmt.text: CONTINUE: Aspirin, clopidogrel and warfarin; limit aspirin to no more than 30 days after PCI.
START: Sacubitril-valsartan, metoprolol succinate, dapagliflozin and atorvastatin.
STOP: Metoprolol tartrate and simvastatin.
CONTINUE: Spironolactone, amiodarone and colchicine.

monitor.text: CHECK: INR and adjust warfarin for interaction with amiodarone.
MONITOR: Creatinine/BMP every 24–48 hours after contrast; BMP every 3 days during HF medication initiation, including the first 2 weeks after ARNI initiation.
REQUEST: NT-proBNP; ICD interrogation for RV pacing burden and CRT-upgrade candidacy.
SAFETY: Bleeding risk with triple antithrombotic therapy; AKI/volume depletion and hyperkalemia risks with combined HF therapies.

dispo.text: FOLLOW-UP: Cardiology in 1–2 weeks for ARNI and beta-blocker titration.

dx.text: DIAGNOSIS: CAD (recorded primary diagnosis); unstable angina and chronic systolic HF also recorded.
HF CHARACTERIZATION: LVEF 25%; global LV hypokinesis.

causes.text: ACTIVE PROBLEMS: Chest pain; three-vessel CAD, patent SVG-LAD graft and occluded SVG-OM graft.
HISTORY: CABG, prior LCx PCI, bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement, ICD, AF and gout.

acute.text: START: IV nitroglycerin titrated for chest pain, aspirin, morphine and hydromorphone before transfer.
PERFORM: Balloon angioplasty of the OM2 origin with less than 20% residual stenosis and normal flow.

gdmt.text: START: Furosemide, warfarin, simvastatin, atorvastatin and colchicine.
START: Sodium chloride, vitamin K1, sitocalciferol, glucose, sodium bicarbonate, acetylcysteine, docusate and sennosides.

monitor.text: OBTAIN: Coronary/graft angiography and hemodynamic assessment; echocardiogram with normally functioning bioprosthetic aortic valve gradient.
OBTAIN: Chest radiograph without signs of overhydration.
MONITOR: No recommendation.

dispo.text: ADMIT: Transferred to the CCU for consideration of cardiac catheterization; chest-pain free on arrival.
